title: Coldprime interleaved surge notes
content:
Quick context / objective:
- Trying to reproduce and characterize a recurring failure mode I started seeing on the staging pool: small client mixes (10-50 qps) where a few cold contexts injected into a warm stream cause short microbursts of 300–800ms P95 spikes even though average throughput is fine.
- Hypothesis: interleaved priming + KV-cache churn is triggering suboptimal batching decisions and GPU kernel fallbacks; dynamic batcher exposes bad latency behaviour when priming requests interleave with steady-state ones.

Cluster & test harness:
- Pool: 1x a100-sxm4 node (8 GPU partition sim) vs g5.12xlarge (for lower-end behavior).
- Runtime branch: PR 342 local build (see linked PR).
- Workload generator: local harness (scripts/run_interleaved_surge.sh) that replays 10k requests with arrival mix: 90% warm (same context id), 10% cold (unique context), Zipf alpha=1.2.
- Sequence lengths: prompt=60 tokens, gen cap=150 tokens.
- Batcher config: dynamic batching enabled, max_batch=64, max_latency_ms=30, interleave=true. Also tested static batching and prefill-only mode.

What I ran (commands to repeat):
- ./run_interleaved_surge.sh --backend=a100 --qps=40 --cold-pct=10 --seed=20250214
- runner records per-request timestamps and labels (COLD/WARM). Aggregates: p50/p95/p99, tail counts >500ms, batch size distribution, KV cache hit ratio.

Raw observations (first-pass):
- Baseline (all-warm, qps=40): p95 ~ 42ms, p99 ~ 65ms, near-zero >500ms events.
- Interleaved (10% cold): p95 jumps to 310ms, p99 ~ 540ms, ~1.7% of requests >500ms. Bursts are localized: 6–12 contiguous requests spike then decay over ~500–1200ms window.
- g5 results: similar pattern but magnitudes higher (p95 ~ 520ms) and more variability.

Metric excerpts (run: a100 interleaved):
- QPS target: 40
- p50 22ms, p95 310ms, p99 538ms
- tail>500ms: 174/10000 (1.74%)
- avg batch size: 12, batch size variance spikes concurrently with tail events
- KV cache hit ratio: drops from 98% -> 86% in the first 2s of a surge window

What I instrumented to understand cause:
- Added per-batch metadata (batch.type: priming/mixed/steady) and recorded kernel selection path (fastpath vs slowpath), and whether quantized kernels were used.
- Correlated batch.type with latency spikes: 92% of tail events come from batches labeled mixed (contain both COLD and WARM requests).
- Mixed batches often trigger a different kernel because sequence-length distribution widened and KV cache state required additional memory ops.

Hypothesis refined:
- Mixed batches force the runtime to allocate extra KV slots and sometimes evict hot entries mid-batch; eviction plus extra memory moves causes kernel fallback that is ~6–8x slower.
- Dynamic batcher tries to fill batches quickly; when a cold request arrives it delays dispatch to coalesce, but the coalescing widens sequence lengths and mixes states, increasing variance.

Quick experiments tried and outcome:
1) Disable interleave (coalesce only identical context ids): reduces p95 to ~60ms, p99 to ~95ms; tail>500ms ~0.05%. Good but reduces throughput slightly.
2) Force prefill-only for cold requests (do prefill pass separate) — p95 ~75ms, p99 ~130ms; reduces mixed-batch tails but increases average token latency for cold ones.
3) KV prewarm heuristic: when a cold request is predicted (based on signature), pre-allocate KV slots asynchronously — improved hit ratio to 95% and p95 ~120ms.
4) Increase max_latency_ms to 80ms (allow larger batching window): reduced p95 in some runs but increased variance and made p99 worse in others because larger batches become mixed more often.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Need to know whether eviction is happening due to global KV capacity or per-GPU limit. Add counters for evictions per-GPU per-batch.
- Is kernel fallback deterministic based on max_seq_in_batch or influenced by memory pressure? Log the selected kernel with exact arguments (seq_len, batch_sz, mem_alloc).
- Consider a policy: route cold/priming requests to a dedicated lane (small pool) to avoid contamination of hot lanes. This mirrors a 'priming pool' idea in earlier notes but needs capacity cost estimates.

Next runs to queue (prio):
- Add eviction counters + kernel arg logging (high priority).
- Run same interleaved pattern with dedicated priming pool (2x small workers) to measure throughput/cost tradeoff.
- Try smaller dynamic-batcher max_batch=32 vs 64 to see if mixed-batch frequency decreases.
- Re-run on g5 with prewarm heuristic to gauge cross-hardware efficacy.

Mini conclusions (so far):
- Interleaving cold priming requests with warm steady traffic is a plausible root for the observed microbursts. Mixed batches that touch KV and widen seq_len distributions correlate strongly with tail events.
- Short-term mitigations: disable interleaving or prefill cold requests separately. Longer-term: smarter prewarm + lightweight priming pool + kernel selection rules.

Links / artifacts to attach to a proper report:
- local run logs: /tmp/astrid/primewave_runs/20250214_interleaved.tar.gz
- perf traces (flamegraphs): s3://redwood-inference-artifacts/primewave/20250214/
- JIRA: JIRA-1284 (triage ticket)

Random musings (notes to self):
- Could explore a lightweight inline prefetch that runs on CPU and loads KV into GPU asynchronously ahead of dispatch — maybe free in many deployments.
- Customer impact: this pattern could leak into bursty product traffic where a small percentage of users trigger long contexts (e.g., long chat threads opening new sessions). Worth writing a short RCA template for CS.

-- astrid
